
'''Katori Shrine''' (香取神社, Katori Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines named "Katori" dedicated to the deity Futsunushi.

There are approximately 400 shrines with this name across Japan, centered primarily around the Kantō region, with the Katori Jingū in Katori, Chiba as their head shrine. Most Katori Shrines were founded as branch shrines of Katori Jingū, sharing the same enshrined deity, Futsunushi.

Their distribution is mainly along the Tone River and Edo River. Along the southern Arakawa River (Kantō) lie Hikawa Shrines, and along the Moto-Arakawa River between them lie Hisaizu Shrines. According to Nishitsunoi Masayoshi, the distribution areas of these shrines are distinct without overlap. The distribution area of Katori Shrines covers former marshland reclaimed from the 10th century onward.
